overview: Coca-Cola HBC AG is an independent, strategic bottling partner of The Coca-Cola Company (TCCC) -- not TCCC itself -- producing, distributing and selling TCCC's trademarked beverages plus a wider 24/7 portfolio (Monster Energy, Costa Coffee, Caffe Vergnano, Finlandia and other brands) across 29 countries spanning Western, Central and Eastern Europe, and Africa. The Group serves roughly 760 million consumers through Established markets (e.g. Italy, Switzerland, Ireland, Greece), Developing markets (e.g. Poland, Hungary, Czech Republic) and Emerging markets (e.g. Nigeria, Egypt, Russia, Romania, Ukraine), and reports in euros. In October 2025 it agreed to acquire a 75% stake in Coca-Cola Beverages Africa (CCBA) for US$2.6bn, a deal expected to complete by end-2026 that would roughly double its African footprint and create the world's second-largest Coca-Cola bottler by volume.

business_model.summary: CCH buys concentrate from The Coca-Cola Company under an incidence-based pricing model, then manufactures, distributes and sells finished beverages to retail, HoReCa and vending customers across its territories. TCCC owns the brands and funds consumer marketing; CCH owns the manufacturing/logistics/route-to-market infrastructure and funds trade marketing, in a long-standing franchise-bottler partnership (CCH's roots as a TCCC bottler date to 1951 in Nigeria and formally as Coca-Cola HBC since 1969 in Greece/2000 London listing). Revenue is transactional (unit-case sales to retailers/distributors/outlets) rather than subscription-based, but it is highly repeatable, non-discretionary, everyday consumption revenue with a long track record of volume and price/mix growth. Customers are overwhelmingly B2B (retailers, wholesalers, HoReCa outlets, vending), serving B2C end consumers indirectly.

business_model.customer_type: B2B (retailers, wholesalers, HoReCa, vending operators) selling to 1.9 million customers and ultimately 760 million consumers
business_model.geographic_mix: 29 countries across Western/Central/Eastern Europe and Africa; segmented as Established 31% of FY2025 revenue (10.5% comparable EBIT margin), Developing 22% (9.5% margin), Emerging 47% (13.5% margin, highest-margin segment). Pending CCBA deal adds 14 African territories (South Africa, Kenya, Mozambique, Uganda, Ethiopia, Tanzania, Zambia and others).

main_competitors: Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP, the other large TCCC bottler in Western Europe/Australasia)
Refresco and other private-label/own-brand beverage producers
Local/regional soft drinks and energy drink challengers in individual markets
Coca-Cola Beverages Africa (CCBA) -- currently a separate TCCC bottler in Africa, being acquired by CCH
competitive_position.market_position: Leading position in Sparkling soft drinks across its 29 markets and a leader in the broader non-alcoholic ready-to-drink (NARTD) category; sixth consecutive year of NARTD value share gains in 2025 (+80bps) and continued share gains in H1 2026 (+80bps NARTD, +40bps Sparkling). Once CCBA completes, CCH becomes the world's second-largest Coca-Cola bottling partner by volume, covering 43 markets across Europe and Africa.

moat_factors.factor: Exclusive territorial bottling franchise with The Coca-Cola Company
moat_factors.description: Long-term (effectively perpetual, renewable) bottling agreements grant exclusive rights to produce and distribute TCCC's trademarked brands in each territory, a structural barrier to entry that is very difficult for a new entrant to replicate

Extensive bottling plants, cold-drink equipment, and direct-store-delivery/route-to-market networks across 29 (soon 43) countries built up over 75 years create a logistics cost advantage competitors would need years and heavy capex to replicate
Access to TCCC's trademark brands plus owned/partnered brands (Monster, Costa Coffee, Finlandia, Adult Sparkling) spanning every consumption occasion and price point, from affordable to premium

Deep retailer relationships, digital B2B ordering platforms (Sirvis, eB2B portal with ~40% YoY growth in active users) and revenue growth management tooling support pricing and mix execution, raising switching costs for customers
Mix of mature Established markets and high-growth Emerging/Developing markets provides a natural hedge, though it also concentrates emerging-market and FX risk

weaknesses: Economically dependent on and contractually subordinate to The Coca-Cola Company, which owns the brands, sets concentrate pricing (incidence-based model) and could in principle alter commercial terms
No pricing power over the core trademark brand portfolio independent of TCCC's global strategy
High exposure to volatile, less liquid emerging/frontier-market currencies (Nigerian Naira, Egyptian Pound, Russian Rouble, Ukrainian Hryvnia) that create translation and transaction risk
Russia and Ukraine operations continue amid war and sanctions risk, requiring a self-sufficient, locally-focused Russian business model
Large pending CCBA integration adds execution risk and will materially increase leverage and emerging-market/FX concentration at completion

growth_drivers: Acquisition of Coca-Cola Beverages Africa (CCBA): a transformational ~US$2.6bn deal for 75% of CCBA (option for remaining 25%), expected to complete H2 2026, adding 14 African territories, >800,000 outlets, 40+ brands and exposure to markets with a combined population over 450 million and favorable demographics (CCBA+Nigeria+Egypt represent ~2/3 of Africa's Coca-Cola system volume and >60% of Africa's GDP); expected to be low-single-digit EPS accretive from the first full year

Strategic priority categories Sparkling, Energy and Coffee: Energy (Monster/Predator/Fury) delivered a 10th consecutive year of double-digit growth (+26.1% organic volume in H1 2026); Coffee refocused on the out-of-home channel with Costa Coffee/Caffe Vergnano (+24.5% OOH volume H1 2026)
Revenue growth management (RGM) and premiumisation/affordability balance: single-serve pack mix, pricing tools (Promo360), and tailored pack architecture driving positive price/mix with volume growth
Digital and AI investment: Sirvis B2B platform, eB2B customer portal (~40% growth in monthly active users), AI-driven RGM and route-to-market, Ignite Naija data initiative in Nigeria
Continued NARTD value-share gains (sixth consecutive year in 2025; further gains in 2026) aided by execution and customer-centric capabilities
Secular NARTD category growth (management's internally projected 4%-6% CAGR 2024-2028 ex-Russia/Ukraine) combined with rising per-capita consumption potential in African/emerging markets
Capex into production capacity, automation, digital/data and energy-efficient coolers supporting medium-term margin expansion (medium-term target: +20-40bps organic comparable EBIT margin per year)

business.risk: Franchisor dependency on The Coca-Cola Company
business.description: CCH's core business is contingent on its bottling agreements and ongoing partnership with TCCC, including concentrate pricing and brand/marketing strategy decisions outside CCH's control

Company-identified principal risk (D5): overestimated synergies, cultural/organizational misalignment, IT/systems incompatibility, talent retention and regulatory complexity could erode expected synergies and distract management from the core business

Russia-Ukraine war, Middle East conflict escalation, and US geopolitical policy shifts create risk to employee safety, supply chain stability and potential for sanctions-driven financial impact (principal risk C1, trend: increasing)
Extreme weather, cyber attacks, and plant-level disruptions could impair the Group's ability to supply customers for an extended period (principal risk B2)

business.risk: Product quality and food safety incidents
business.description: Contamination or quality incidents could trigger recalls, consumer harm claims and reputational damage (principal risk B3)
Competition for skilled talent amid digital transformation and flexible-work expectations (principal risk C3)

financial.risk: Foreign exchange volatility across many emerging/frontier currencies
financial.description: Principal risk A1: exposure to Nigerian Naira, Egyptian Pound, Russian Rouble, Ukrainian Hryvnia, Hungarian Forint and others; CCH targets hedging 25%-80% of rolling 12-month FX exposure, but residual volatility affects reported revenue, costs and repatriation of cash; FY2026 guidance shows swings in translational FX impact on EBIT (from a EUR0-30m headwind to a EUR0-10m tailwind over the course of the year)

financial.risk: Rising leverage from CCBA acquisition financing
financial.description: Acquisition funded via a EUR1.4bn bridge facility (now refinanced via bonds issued March 2026) plus shares to Gutsche Family Investments; net debt/EBITDA guided to stay within the 1.5x-2.0x medium-term target range post-completion versus 0.7x-0.8x currently, and net finance cost guidance for FY2026 was raised twice (to EUR40-50m by H1 2026) to reflect CCBA-related bond costs

Sugar, PET/aluminium packaging, and energy costs are exposed to commodity markets and climate-related agricultural productivity risk; rPET costs have risen as the Group increased recycled content (D2 principal risk)

financial.risk: Cash repatriation limits in emerging markets
financial.description: Hard currency liquidity constraints in certain emerging markets could limit the Group's ability to repatriate cash generated locally

regulatory.risk: Sugar taxes and other discriminatory product regulation
regulatory.description: Principal risk D1: governments increasingly use sugar/beverage taxes, marketing restrictions and nutrition regulation to address public health and budgetary pressures; risk trend flagged as increasing with moderate residual risk tolerance; EU priorities include Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation, Deforestation Regulation and expanding Deposit Return Systems (DRS now active in 10 of CCH's markets)

Principal risk A2: operations in/near Russia and Belarus carry risk of inadvertent non-compliance with evolving EU/international sanctions regimes, with potential for significant fines and reputational damage

regulatory.risk: Sustainable packaging and EU regulatory burden
regulatory.description: Principal risk D2/D3: increasing EU regulation on plastics, packaging waste, recycled content requirements and carbon pricing mechanisms are expected to raise input costs over time

Deal requires antitrust clearance across six jurisdictions; as of H1 2026 four of six jurisdictions (Mozambique, Namibia, Botswana, COMESA) had cleared, with South Africa and Tanzania still pending; the South African Competition Commission recommended conditional approval in July 2026 including conditions on retrenchments and downstream investment commitments

macro.description: Elevated cost of living in several markets continues to pressure disposable income, prompting consumers toward smaller pack sizes and value channels, though NARTD is relatively resilient as an affordable treat category

Company's own outlook flags continuing FX volatility driven by US Dollar strength and idiosyncratic emerging-market conditions, particularly in Nigeria, Egypt and Russia; CCBA will add further sub-Saharan African macro exposure (South Africa, Kenya, Ethiopia, Mozambique)

macro.risk: Climate change physical and transition risk
macro.description: Water stress at a subset of plants, agricultural input productivity risk for sugar-growing regions, and rising insurance/carbon costs are identified but currently assessed as low-to-moderate residual risk with multi-year mitigation capex plans

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Management's internal projections put NARTD category value CAGR at 4%-6% for 2024-2028 (ex-Russia/Ukraine); 2025 NARTD growth was driven by higher value per unit case and positive Africa volume growth, with Energy the best-performing category
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate -- non-alcoholic beverages are a relatively defensive consumer staple/affordable treat, but value per case and premiumisation are sensitive to disposable income and inflation; CCH's broad geographic and channel mix provides some cycle diversification
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate and rising -- net finance costs guidance for FY2026 increased from EUR25-45m to EUR40-65m range over the year mainly due to CCBA acquisition bond financing; the Group otherwise maintains a diversified, largely investment-grade funding base (EUR5.0bn EMTN programme, EUR1.0bn commercial paper programme, EUR1.2bn RCF)
macro_factors.currency_exposure: Extensive -- EUR reporting currency against Nigerian Naira, Egyptian Pound, Russian Rouble, Ukrainian Hryvnia, Hungarian Forint, Polish Zloty, Swiss Franc and (pending CCBA) South African Rand, Kenyan Shilling and other African currencies; hedges 25%-80% of rolling 12-month FX exposure but residual volatility is material and flagged as the top-ranked principal risk (A1)
key_input_costs: PET resin and recycled PET (rPET, priced at a premium to virgin PET)
Concentrate (purchased from TCCC under incidence-based pricing)

recent_developments.event: Announced agreement to acquire 75% of Coca-Cola Beverages Africa (CCBA) from The Coca-Cola Company and Gutsche Family Investments for a combined ~US$2.6bn (implied 100% equity value ~US$3.4bn), with an option over the remaining 25%; intends a secondary listing on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange at/around completion
Shareholders approved all resolutions relating to the CCBA acquisition at an Extraordinary General Meeting

Reported FY2025 net sales revenue of EUR11,604.5m (+7.9% reported, +8.1% organic), comparable EBIT of EUR1,356.2m (11.7% margin), comparable EPS of EUR2.724 (+19.7%), free cash flow of EUR700.0m, net debt/comparable EBITDA of 0.7x; proposed dividend of EUR1.20/share (+17%, 44% payout ratio)
Issued bonds to cover the EUR1.4bn cash consideration for the CCBA acquisition, refinancing the earlier bridge facility

Q1 2026 trading update: organic revenue growth of 11.6% (reported +12.0%), organic volume +9.6% (boosted ~6pp by four extra selling days), driven by Emerging markets (+15.0% organic revenue); reiterated FY2026 guidance (organic revenue growth 6%-7%, organic EBIT growth 7%-10%); four of six antitrust jurisdictions cleared for CCBA deal

South African Competition Commission recommended the Competition Tribunal approve the CCBA transaction, subject to conditions (including a moratorium on retrenchments and commitments to downstream distribution/retail investment)

Partnered with The Coca-Cola Company on FIFA World Cup activations across markets (special-edition packs, Panini promotions, fan experiences) as a major marketing driver of H1 2026 volume growth
CCBA acquisition remains on track for completion in H2 2026, pending remaining antitrust/merger clearances in South Africa and Tanzania

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Zoran Bogdanovic described H1 2026 as volume-led, broad-based growth across all three segments, citing FIFA World Cup activations, Monster/Powerade innovation and continued share gains, while flagging that the macroeconomic and geopolitical backdrop remains challenging and unpredictable. Management reiterated confidence in the 24/7 portfolio, bespoke capabilities and people to continue winning share, and explicitly raised full-year revenue and EBIT guidance on the back of H1 strength. The CCBA acquisition was reaffirmed as on track for H2 2026 completion, with South African regulatory conditions (anti-retrenchment moratorium, downstream investment commitments) accepted as part of the approval process.

bull_case: Transformational CCBA acquisition roughly doubles CCH's African exposure, creating the world's second-largest Coca-Cola bottler by volume with access to markets with favorable long-term demographics (population growth, low per-capita consumption, young populations) and is expected to be EPS-accretive from year one

Consistent multi-year track record of organic revenue growth (5th consecutive year of strong growth in 2025) and NARTD value-share gains (6th consecutive year in 2025, continuing into 2026), with FY2026 guidance raised twice this year on H1 strength

High-margin, fast-growing Emerging segment (13.5% comparable EBIT margin in FY2025, highest of the three segments) is driving disproportionate profit growth (+23.9% organic EBIT in H1 2026) as Energy and Sparkling scale in Africa and other emerging markets

Strong balance sheet discipline and shareholder returns -- net debt/EBITDA of 0.7x pre-CCBA, a progressive dividend (+17% to EUR1.20/share for FY2025, within a 40-50% payout target), and ROIC expansion to 19.4% in FY2025

Secular, structurally advantaged bottling franchise with TCCC provides a durable moat (exclusive territorial rights, concentrate supply relationship, brand access) that is difficult for a new entrant to replicate, supporting steady recurring-style demand for an everyday consumer staple
bear_case: CCBA integration carries real execution risk -- management itself flags overestimated synergies, cultural misalignment, IT/systems incompatibility and talent-retention risk as a principal risk, and the deal materially raises leverage (net debt/EBITDA guided up to the 1.5x-2.0x range from ~0.7x) and emerging/frontier-market currency exposure (South Africa, Kenya, Mozambique, Ethiopia, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia)

Heavy and growing reliance on volatile emerging-market currencies (Naira, Egyptian Pound, Rouble, Hryvnia, and soon Rand/Kenyan Shilling) creates persistent translation and transaction FX risk that management can only partially hedge (25%-80% of rolling 12-month exposure)

No independent control over its core brand portfolio or concentrate pricing -- CCH's profitability and strategic flexibility remain structurally subordinate to The Coca-Cola Company's global brand and pricing decisions

Regulatory risk from sugar taxes, EU packaging/plastics regulation and Deposit Return System rollouts is explicitly flagged by management as an increasing trend risk that could raise costs and pressure volumes/mix over the medium term

Geopolitical exposure to active conflict zones (continued Russian operations amid sanctions risk, Ukraine war disruption, and Middle East instability affecting Egypt) adds tail risk beyond normal emerging-market volatility
